newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. signs food aid deal with Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. signs food aid deal with Angola.

text.p: The United Nations' World Food Programme has signed an agreement with the Angolan government to supply some 96,000 tonnes of food aid worth $68 million to the country this year.

Mohamed Zejjari, the director for Africa for the World Food Programme (WFP), said a parallel food assistance programme to supply some 18,000 tonnes of food worth $11 million to demobilised soldiers, had also been signed.

"Although the situation is getting better in Angola, the country is still going through a transition period and still needs some assistance," Zejjari said on the final day of a three day visit to Angola.

WFP Angola country director, Ramiro Lopes da Silva, said the current agreements with the government may be adjusted after a planned Food and Agricultural Organsiation (FAO) study mission to the country next month.

"We know the rains have not been very good this year in parts of the country," said da Silva. "This year should be similar if not worst than last year and we had a shortfall last year. But we will be able to get a clearer picture after the FAO visit."

Zejjari said WFP was looking to move away from emergency food aid into development, with an eye toward increasing a number of food-for-work programmes already underway that aim to rebuild the war shattered infrastructure.

In 1996 the WFP shipped over 115,000 tonnes of U.N. food aid into Angola, down from 200,000 tonnes in 1995. Beneficiaries of WFP food assistance have fallen from 2.2 million in November 1994 to 650,000 today, according to WFP officials.
